scope: Byte reproduction of selected Unicode files, not full Perl/native-build or redistribution acceptance.

ucdEquivalence.explanation: mktables builds @inline_definitions by pushing onto it while iterating a Perl hash; hash iteration order is PERL_HASH_SEED-randomized per process since Perl 5.18, so separate build runs reorder that array and every numeric #/N index into it without changing any resolved value. This check resolves every index in both files and compares sorted, fully-resolved (hash, key, value) records.

observations: The first flattened invocation changed the generated header because mktables records its invocation path. Invoking the unchanged script as lib/unicore/mktables with -C lib/unicore reproduces the original header; no output rewriting is used.
Seventeen Scx payload files exactly match generated Sc files. Their path mappings are recorded rather than silently renamed.

UCD.pl differs byte-for-byte in the ordering of its @inline_definitions array and every numeric #/N index into it, because mktables builds that array while iterating a Perl hash and hash iteration order is PERL_HASH_SEED-randomized per process since Perl 5.18. Resolving every index in both files and comparing sorted, fully-resolved (hash, key, value) records (applying the one documented Sc/Scx alias above) confirms semantic equivalence; see ucdEquivalence. It remains an unmatched byte, and its exact original generation environment/hash seed is not recoverable.

The source is Perl 5.32.1 with Unicode 13.0.0 data; the developer interpreter is system Perl v5.34.1. This is successful byte reproduction for the matched subset, not a reproduction of the full original Biber build.

Initial default-deny read-scoped profiles aborted during macOS dyld startup before Perl ran. The final developer-only profile permits reads and system operations, denies networking and limits file writes. Controls require real EPERM for outside writes and a loopback connection.
